evals.prompt: In the attached demo app, add Conqueror in-process messaging for creating todos. Define a CreateTodo message with a response containing the created id, implement the handler using the existing TodoStore, register handlers in DI, add an endpoint or service call that uses IMessageSenders.For(CreateTodo.T), and add tests that exercise the behavior through Conqueror rather than directly constructing the handler.
evals.expected_output: A working implementation using partial Conqueror message contracts, generated handler interfaces, DI registration, IMessageSenders.For(CreateTodo.T), and tests through the public Conqueror factory.
expectations: Defines a partial CreateTodo message contract using a Conqueror message attribute
Implements a partial handler via the generated CreateTodo.IHandler interface
Invokes the message through IMessageSenders.For(CreateTodo.T)
Registers Conqueror message handlers in dependency injection
Adds or updates tests that exercise the Conqueror invocation path rather than only direct handler construction

evals.prompt: In the attached demo app, expose todo lookup over HTTP using Conqueror. Add an HTTP-capable GetTodo message with a response DTO, wire ASP.NET Core server registration and endpoint mapping, add a client-side usage example with UseHttp, and cover the behavior with an appropriate test. Keep package versions consistent with the fixture and do not hard-code unrelated versions in explanatory text.
evals.expected_output: HTTP Conqueror message usage with [HttpMessage<T>], server registration/mapping, client transport selection, and test coverage.
expectations: Defines an HTTP-capable partial message contract using HttpMessage
Adds ASP.NET Core server setup for Conqueror HTTP endpoints
Uses IMessageSenders.For(GetTodo.T).WithTransport(...UseHttp...) for client-side invocation
Mentions or implements serializer-context/AOT considerations when relevant
Adds tests or a testable setup that validates the HTTP-facing behavior

evals.prompt: In the attached demo app, publish a TodoCreated signal after a todo is created and add a signal handler that updates metrics. Use a Conqueror pipeline or context data to prevent double-counting within one operation if the signal is observed more than once. Add tests that prove the signal path updates metrics and does not double-count.
evals.expected_output: Signal contract, publisher usage, signal handler registration, context/pipeline guard, and tests through ISignalPublishers or a message that publishes the signal.
expectations: Defines a partial TodoCreated signal contract
Publishes via ISignalPublishers.For(TodoCreated.T).Handle(...)
Implements a partial signal handler via TodoCreated.IHandler
Uses Conqueror context or pipeline logic for the double-counting guard
Adds tests proving signal side effects and the guard behavior
